Elizabeth.wildlife_intro:
Our crew's Elizabeth calls follow the ground the town sits on: little Kanawha River (along the town), wooded ridges rising around the valley, historic courthouse-town core on the bottom. That setting puts raccoons, gray squirrels, bats, opossums in regular contact with homes here, and most jobs start with a full roofline and foundation inspection, then removal and sealing every entry we find. Every operator we send is a WVDNR-licensed Wildlife Damage Control Agent (WDCA), and we handle disposition the West Virginia way — exclusion and on-site liberation where the rules allow it, never a relocation promise.

In fall and winter, squirrels and rodents push into warm attics across the county, and spring brings denning raccoons looking for chimneys and soffits to raise young. Elizabeth is a small historic river town of 1800s homes and quiet streets. Call us at (844) 544-3498 when you first hear scratching or find droppings or digging — early jobs are almost always simpler jobs.
